companies.latest_signal: Core local commerce swung back to a RMB5.67bn operating profit in Q2 2026 (margin +7.9%) as management says subsidy policy is being '持续优化' and competition is shifting from cash-burn to efficiency/experience, but they also flagged Q3 2026 unit economics will face seasonal headwinds (delivery costs, marketing) and full normalization vs. 2024 subsidy levels will take several more quarters.

companies.latest_signal: Management (CEC head Jiang Fan) says Taobao Flash Sale's per-order loss and unit economics are improving sequentially 'faster than expected,' targeting UE breakeven by end of FY2027 and group EBITA breakeven around FY2029, but the Q2 2026 near-flat EBITA figure is partly a segment-definition effect (AIDC and Freshippo, both improving/profitable, were merged in), and internal leadership has told teams to keep spending aggressively on Flash Sale through all of 2026 to defend ~45% share against Meituan — so the underlying subsidy war is not over even as the disclosed drag narrows.

companies.latest_signal: JD says total food-delivery investment fell over 50% YoY in Q2 2026 and New Businesses revenue dropped 47.6% YoY as the 2025 subsidy blitz lapped itself; group Non-GAAP profit rose 20.3% YoY even as top-line growth slowed, and CEO Xu Ran reiterated JD isn't reacting to rivals' 'micro-moves,' signaling a deliberate subsidy pullback rather than a demand problem.

war_summary: All three platforms have cut cash-burn intensity since regulators (SAMR's 'anti-involution'/反内卷 campaign) pressured the sector from mid-2025 onward, and each company's own loss proxy has now improved for 2-3 consecutive quarters off Q3 2025 peaks — Meituan flipped core local commerce back to profit, JD's delivery-specific spend is down over half YoY, and Alibaba's disclosed EBITA drag has shrunk sharply (though partly flattered by June-2026 segment reshuffling). Meituan is signaling it wants the sector to '回归理性,' JD says it won't chase competitors, but Alibaba's leadership has told its team to keep spending hard on Taobao Flash Sale through 2026 to defend near-45% instant-retail share — so pure food-delivery subsidies are cooling faster than the broader instant-commerce (non-food/Flash Sale) fight, where Alibaba still looks like the side least willing to blink first.
